standards.name: Global Internal Audit Standards (GIAS) in the UK Public Sector
standards.quote: From 1st April 2025 the Public Sector Internal Auditing Standards will be replaced by the Global Internal Audit Standards (GIAS) in the UK Public Sector. These new standards still require the Council’s Audit Plan and Internal Audit Charter to be approved by the Governance Committee. A new requirement is for there to be an Internal Audit Strategy which requires review with senior managers and the Governance Committee (no formal approval required).

risk_based_plan.quote: 5.7 The Internal Audit work programme for the period 202 5-2028 is attached at Appendix D. The plan analyses the different areas of the Council’s activity that Internal Audit have determined need to be audited after carrying out a risk assessment process. The Plan is broken down by Corporate Audits, then by Executive Director, and Service Director. The information for each audit covers: - (a) The key risks involved in that area. (b) The level of risk associated with the audit area/function, as assessed by I nternal Audit. (c) The type of audit , setting out any direct links with the Council Strategy and Corporate Risk Register. (d) Date last reviewed. (e) An initial estimate of the number of days that will be required to complete the audit, and the year in which the audit is planned/last audited.

team.quote: The Audit Team consists of five staff; the Audit Manager, a Principal Auditor, two Senior Auditors and one Auditor post. This level of resource has been used to set out the plan of work over the three-year period.

performance_target.metric: at least 80% of the audit plan for the year

risk_themes.quote: The Council aims to operate with a financial risk between £250k – £500k.

The Council aims to operate with a legal risk that finely balanced between flexible and open, following approved standards and practices as far as possible but also allowing for innovation, willing to engage in new areas of work, of significant public interest, and related to high value transactions.

risk_themes.relevance_reason: Corporate governance and reputation context for contracts.
risk_themes.quote: The Council’s reputation is one of the most important assets which employees and Councillors aim to protect to ensure there is little chance of significant repercussions. This relates primarily to the core business areas. As custodians of the public’s trust and public’s funds, even the transformational activities are delivered with sound governance arrangements in place and follow a strong and consistent corporate project management methodology. However, in the process of seeking the benefits of new ways of achieving or improving outcomes for the residents the Council is seeking an open reputational risk, with possible significant reputational damage or enhancement.

risk_themes.relevance_reason: Explicit contractor delivery and procurement contract management risk source.
risk_themes.quote: Dependency on, or failure of, contractors to deliver services or products to the agreed cost and specification. Procurement contract and relationship management. Overall partnership arrangements, e.g. for pooled budgets or community safety. PFI, LSVT and regeneration.

scoring_method.selection_note: Response bands use Table 4 (p.19): Extreme 15–25, Medium - High 8–12, Moderate 4–6, Low up to 3. Figure 4 (p.21) separately states Corporate Risk Register inclusion at score 9 or above. The discrepancy is preserved, not silently resolved; auditor review is required.

evaluation_levels.definition: Likelihood and impact without additional, specific mitigation action.
evaluation_levels.quote: Gross level – likelihood and impact without additional, specific mitigation action.

evaluation_levels.definition: Current likelihood and impact with implemented mitigation, excluding planned mitigation.
evaluation_levels.quote: Actual level - this is the current likelihood and impact, based on mitigation action already put in place but excluding further mitigation action planned.

evaluation_levels.definition: Future likelihood and impact with additional planned mitigation.
evaluation_levels.quote: Expected level – this is a future level of likelihood and impact based on any additional mitigation action (if any) planned to further address the triggers and the consequences of risks.
